title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Shelf-Tag Flyer. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Shelf-Tag Flyer
options.lineage: Canadian weekly grocery flyers and shelf price tags
options.thesis: Every number that matters is a shelf tag you can read from across the aisle.
options.viewport: A flyer-yellow top bar and rail; Safe to spend as one giant shelf tag with its per-day price, budget tags beside it, plain white tables below.
options.risk: Reads discount-store if yellow floods the content; it stays in the shell and the tags.

raised.raise: Every tag prints its change since last month beside the number, on one strict neutral ramp.
Size is rank: a fixed figure-size ramp, so the most important number is the biggest one on screen.
Chrome deleted: no boxed cards; big numbers and colour fields do the organising.
One visible cell grid: tags and tables snap to whole cells and reflow by cell on phones.

options.label: Polymer Banknotes
options.thesis: Each category is a denomination: its own colour, engraved line work and a clear window.
options.viewport: A clear-window Safe to spend panel with fine engraved lines; category budgets as note-coloured strips.
options.risk: The familiar move for money apps, and five note colours turn busy without strict discipline.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Each budget is a line; the month is the route and today is your station.
options.viewport: Budget lines run left to right across the month with today's station ringed; Safe to spend is the next stop.
options.case: Canadians read transit maps daily and the month-as-route maps cleanly; its midnight ground clashes with your no-dark rule, so it would be built light.
options.risk: Lines get crowded past six budgets.

options.label: Gate Board
options.thesis: Money as departures: bills and spending ranked by when they leave, changes held lit until seen.
options.viewport: A departures board of upcoming bills by due date beside a segmented pass showing Safe to spend.
options.case: Clearest for what is coming next; weaker for budgets, and the travel metaphor is borrowed.
options.risk: Reads like an airline tool if the board leads every page.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over an eleven-step zone ramp.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets with hatch density per region.
options.case: Few households identify with darkroom craft, and hatching hides the plain numbers.
options.kept: Every figure carries its change since last month.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Amounts as stars on a navy chart.
options.viewport: A navy sky of spending stars.
options.case: Dark night-sky ground breaks your no-dark rule and turns money into decoration.
options.kept: Size is rank: the most important number is the biggest.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant cropped lowercase on flat tiles.
options.viewport: A black panorama of live tiles.
options.case: Black ground and neon tiles are the dark, techy look you ruled out.
options.kept: Chrome deleted: numbers and colour fields organise, not boxes.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: A visible grid with monumental figures.
options.case: A poster discipline, not a money world households recognise.
options.kept: One visible cell grid that reflows by whole cells.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern budgeting app executed impeccably: white cards, one brand colour, clean charts.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, a row of KPI cards, a chart and a transactions list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other budgeting app by design.
